title: Detect when full-product mass cannot certify molecular sequence order
statement: If an observation depends only on the counts of four canonical monomer types in a fixed-length chain with the same termini, distinct orders with the same composition are indistinguishable. At length4 there are256 ordered sequences and35 composition classes; the24 permutations containing one of each monomer share the same composition-only mass. Correct full mass is therefore insufficient to certify sequence order or bond site.

requires: Plain canonical monomer identities, fixed chain length and termini, and an observation depending only on composition/additive molecular mass.
Any added sequence/site-sensitive assay must be specified as a new observation interface.
provides: If an observation depends only on the counts of four canonical monomer types in a fixed-length chain with the same termini, distinct orders with the same composition are indistinguishable. At length4 there are256 ordered sequences and35 composition classes; the24 permutations containing one of each monomer share the same composition-only mass. Correct full mass is therefore insufficient to certify sequence order or bond site.
assumptions: The count argument is exact; actual mass resolution, adducts, modifications, fragmentation spectra and sequence-specific chemistry are different interfaces.
This does not refute established sequence-dependent readout methods or show that35 compositions always give distinct measured peaks.
costs: Additional sequence/junction/end-group information is required; full mass alone retains a24-way order ambiguity in the one-of-each class. No actual analytical instrument or measured sequence validation is acquired.
contract.units: Sequence/class counts are dimensionless; the composition-only mass map uses one declared mass unit. No resolution assumption removes within-composition aliases.
contract.obstruction: Acquire actual sequence/site-resolving product observations before treating a mass-correct product as an instruction-correct product.

body: The observation factors through the count vector (n_A,n_C,n_G,n_T), with sum4. Stars-and-bars gives binomial(7,3)=35 possible vectors; a class has4!/(n_A!*n_C!*n_G!*n_T!) sequences. The class-size histogram is1:4,4:12,6:6,12:12,24:1 and totals256. For instance ACGT and AGCT alias. The same factorization obstruction holds even with perfect mass precision or downstream processing of that mass alone; richer sequence-dependent fragmentation/ladders and site/end-group assays add a different input and are not excluded. Mass may fail to separate even some different compositions, so35 is the number of composition classes, not a promise of35 resolved mass peaks.
